title: Brown Rice with Vegetables and Gravy

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice with vegetables and gravy is a dish that combines whole‑grain brown rice, sautéed vegetables (carrot, broccoli, bell pepper) and a flavorful gravy made from tomatoes and spices. The meal is rich in fiber, vitamins and minerals while providing a moderate amount of fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains the bran and germ, giving it more nutrients than white rice.
The vegetables add not only taste but also antioxidants such as beta‑carotene and vitamin C.
Gravy is often based on tomato puree, a good source of lycopene.
The dish is popular in Asian cuisine, served as a side or a main course.
When stored properly, brown rice can stay fresh for up to 6 months.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Brown rice provides thiamine, niacin and vitamin B6, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains magnesium and iron
items.content: These minerals aid muscle function, nervous system health and blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidant vegetables
items.content: Broccoli and bell pepper are rich in vitamin C and polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: The gravy adds a small amount of fat, which can be part of a balanced diet when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Sodium in the gravy
items.content: Prepared gravy can be high in salt, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to specific vegetables or spices used in the dish.

items.title: Digestive issues from excess fiber
items.content: Consuming large amounts of brown rice may cause bloating or discomfort in those with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a standalone meal or as a side to meat, fish, or tofu. It reheats well in the microwave or on a skillet, adding a splash of water to keep it moist.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze portions in bags at –18 °C and reheat thoroughly before eating.
